every recommendation of a preferred or higher-paying option is accompanied by an alternative and a recorded rationale expressed in the client's own brief terms
revisit_triggers: a new incentive appears, such as a bonus programme, override or production tier
a client expresses surprise about how the advisor is paid
a review of proposals shows preferred options dominating regardless of brief

base.update_signal: a new compensation arrangement enters the practice, or a client reaction shows the existing disclosure was not understood

nodes.definition: Write the practice's standing answer for work that earns nothing from a supplier, because these requests arrive constantly and an unwritten policy collapses under the first sympathetic case. The recurring categories: point-to-point air tickets, award and points redemptions the client already holds, small independent hotel stays that pay little or nothing, restaurant and activity logistics, itinerary review of a trip somebody else built, and passport, visa and documentation legwork. The options for each are to decline it with a plain explanation, to charge a fee that reflects the time it takes, to fold it into a broader engagement whose fee already covers it, or to absorb it deliberately as goodwill for an established client within a stated limit. The policy must be written per category, applied consistently, and quotable to a client in one sentence, because the alternative is an advisor quietly working unpaid hours on the requests that arrive with the most emotional pressure - a friend, a family member, a long-standing client's adult child. Where an advisor chooses to absorb work, that choice belongs in the fee model and the capacity budget rather than in a moment of reluctance to say no.

included: the recurring non-paying request categories
the four handling options and the per-category rule
the consistency and goodwill-limit discipline
excluded: commission tracking for the components that do pay

pros.claim: A written per-category rule survives emotional pressure that an ad-hoc judgement does not
pros.example: a consistent answer to a long-standing client's request for an unpaid award-ticket rebooking, given the same way to everyone

pros.claim: Pricing non-commissionable work makes valuable service possible instead of refusing it outright
pros.example: charging a service fee for an air-only itinerary the advisor is genuinely better at building than the client is

cons.claim: Charging for work travelers can attempt themselves invites comparison with doing it free online
cons.example: a client questioning a service fee for a ticket they could book on an airline site in ten minutes

cons.claim: A strict policy can damage a valuable long-term relationship over a small unpaid request
cons.example: declining a fifteen-minute favour for a client who has booked substantial travel for years

failure_modes: having no policy and absorbing unpaid work in proportion to how insistent the asker is
applying the policy inconsistently between friends and strangers, which becomes visible
charging for the work without stating in advance what it includes
absorbing goodwill work without counting it against capacity
acceptance_tests: each non-commissionable request category has a written handling rule and a one-sentence client explanation
goodwill work absorbed in a period is recorded and counted against the practice's capacity budget
revisit_triggers: unpaid work rises as a share of the practice's hours
a category shifts from paying to non-paying, or the reverse, in supplier terms
clients repeatedly push back on one specific category's rule

base.update_signal: a period's record of unpaid hours by request category shows the policy is not holding

nodes.definition: Set truthful expectations about price and value against the option every client already has, which is booking it themselves in a browser. The honest position separates three cases. Sometimes the advisor's rate is genuinely the same, because supplier pricing is parity-controlled, and what differs is what comes with it or who answers when it goes wrong. Sometimes the advisor can offer something the client cannot get alone - a programme amenity, a value-add, a room or cabin category held for the trade, an operator who does not sell direct - and that difference should be stated specifically rather than gestured at. And sometimes an aggregator, a flash sale or the client's own loyalty status will simply be cheaper, and the honest answer is to say so and let the client decide whether the advisory work is worth its cost. What the practice never does is claim it is always cheaper, imply that booking direct is reckless, or use disruption stories as a pressure device. The value that can be claimed truthfully is concrete: time returned, choices narrowed by someone who knows the product, mistakes prevented, and a named person to reach when a supplier's call centre will not help.

included: the three honest cases of rate comparison
what value may be claimed and how to state it specifically
the prohibition on always-cheaper claims and fear-based positioning

pros.claim: Naming the case where the client can do better alone builds the credibility that makes the other cases believable
pros.example: telling a client their airline status will beat anything the practice can arrange for that flight, then designing the rest of the trip

pros.claim: Specific value statements survive scrutiny in a way that general claims about service do not
pros.example: stating exactly which amenity applies on a qualifying booking instead of promising better treatment

cons.claim: Honesty about parity pricing removes the simplest sales argument and forces the advisor to justify the fee on advisory value alone
cons.example: a rate-shopping prospect leaving once told the hotel rate is identical to what they found

cons.claim: Clients accustomed to discount promises may read candour as weakness or lack of access
cons.example: a prospect assuming the advisor lacks connections because they did not promise a lower price

failure_modes: claiming or implying that the advisor is always cheaper
using disruption and worst-case stories as the reason to book through the practice
promising vague better treatment that no supplier has agreed to provide
staying silent when the client's own status or an aggregator plainly offers more
acceptance_tests: the practice's stated value proposition contains no always-cheaper claim and no fear-based framing
in a live comparison the advisor can say which of the three cases applies and support it with a specific, verifiable difference
revisit_triggers: a supplier changes parity rules or trade-only inventory in a category the practice sells
clients repeatedly raise the same online-price objection the current explanation does not answer
a promised value-add fails to materialise for a client

base.update_signal: the objections clients actually raise, and whether promised value-adds were delivered, over a season of proposals

nodes.definition: Build the arithmetic that says whether the chosen model, niche and fee schedule can actually carry the practice, using the practice's own contract terms rather than any published average. The computation has four inputs the advisor must measure rather than guess: the hours a trip of each type consumes end to end, including discovery, research, revisions, booking, documentation and the support hours a live trip demands; the number of such trips the advisor can carry in a period at that hour load alongside marketing, administration and commission reconciliation; the revenue mechanisms each trip type activates under the practice's own split and fee schedule; and the fixed costs that arrive regardless of bookings - affiliation or accreditation, consortium dues, coverage, technology, marketing, credential renewals. Run against a realistic year and again against a bad one. What the arithmetic produces is not a forecast but three operating decisions: the intake limit beyond which service quality will fail, the fee floor below which a trip type is not worth taking, and the trip types the practice should stop selling. Because every input is practice-specific and every contract differs, the output is a mechanism the advisor recomputes, never a number to be copied from anyone.

included: measured hours per trip type
fixed-cost inventory
the intake limit, fee floor and drop-list decisions the arithmetic produces

pros.claim: Measured hours turn a vague sense of being busy into a defensible intake limit
pros.example: discovering that multi-country itineraries consume several times the hours of a repeat cruise booking, which changes what the practice accepts in peak season

pros.claim: Running the arithmetic on a bad year exposes fixed costs that only look affordable in a good one
pros.example: consortium dues, coverage and technology renewals landing in a season when enquiries stalled

cons.claim: Hour measurement is tedious and advisors systematically under-record the fragmented support time a live trip consumes
cons.example: an hour log that omits the fifteen-minute interruptions across a client's travel week

cons.claim: The arithmetic can argue for dropping a trip type that carries strategic or referral value beyond its own margin
cons.example: a low-margin repeat trip type that consistently introduces the practice to new families

failure_modes: using someone else's published averages instead of the practice's own contract terms and measured hours
counting only design hours and ignoring support, admin and reconciliation time
modelling only a good year
producing the numbers and then ignoring the intake limit they imply
acceptance_tests: the model is built from the practice's own measured hours, its own split and fee terms, and its own quoted fixed costs, with a downside year run alongside the realistic one
the output states an explicit intake limit, a fee floor per trip type and any trip types the practice will stop selling
revisit_triggers: the fee schedule, host terms or fixed costs change
measured hours per trip type drift from the model's assumptions
service quality signals slip, which usually means the intake limit was breached before it was noticed

base.update_signal: a period of recorded hours and actual collected revenue per trip type replaces the estimates the model was built on

edges.why_related: which registration classes have to be checked depends on what the practice says it sells, where it sells it and whether it takes client money
affiliation is only assessable against the revenue mechanisms and the service depth the frame committed to
the fixed costs of independence can only be judged worthwhile against the volume and revenue mechanisms the frame describes
the niche must be able to carry the revenue mechanism the practice chose, so the frame precedes the concentration decision
entity form, client-money handling and record retention are shaped by the registration and client-funds classes that were found to apply
what the advisor may say about protection is the sharpest edge of the advice boundary, so the licensing class defines part of the boundary
the diligence questions are derived from what affiliation is supposed to supply and charge for
under affiliation the host holds the accreditation the booking is written under, which is the fact that sets the whole payment path
owning the accreditation removes a party from the payment path, so the independent choice rewrites the same structural map
for most affiliated advisors programme access arrives through the host's membership rather than through a direct one
the exit, data-ownership and non-solicitation terms are read during diligence, which is the only moment they can still be negotiated
a candidate niche must exist and be stated before there is anything to test for reachable buyers and commissionable suppliers
leverage accrues only where the niche has a countable set of suppliers the practice can concentrate production with
the clientele axis of the niche is what makes an observable served profile and a decline list writable
the referable sentence and the communities to anchor in follow from who the practice actually serves
the fee model is designed to sit on top of a known commission path, including the components of a trip that pay nothing
joining a preferred programme creates the incentive that the disclosure rule exists to make visible
the revenue side of the capacity arithmetic is whatever the fee schedule and split actually collect per trip type
whether the host's registration covers the affiliated advisor constrains whether affiliation resolves the obligation or merely relocates it
an enquiry that can only be served well by interpreting coverage must be declined or routed if the practice does not hold the licensing class
the duty of care forbids the fear-based and urgency framings that are the easiest way to win a price comparison
earned supplier standing may inform which suppliers the practice serves well, but disclosure bounds how it may show up in a recommendation
charging client-paid fees can interact with registration and client-funds obligation classes, so the verified answer bounds the fee design
the intake limit the arithmetic produces is what turns the decline list from a preference into an operating limit
a fee charged before design work protects the practice's time but removes prospects the profile would otherwise have welcomed
edges.resolution_rule: keep the fee and let it filter, but only after the practice has enough enquiry flow to survive the filtering; while flow is thin, reduce the scope the fee buys rather than dropping the fee, so pricing stays consistent across clients

edges.why_related: programme production expectations pull toward preferred suppliers while the disclosure rule requires recommendations to be defensible on the client's brief alone
edges.resolution_rule: the client brief decides the recommendation and the disclosure is always made; if programme production expectations can only be met by recommending against the brief, reduce or exit the programme rather than bend the recommendation

edges.why_related: the same practice cannot simultaneously buy infrastructure with a commission share and keep the whole commission with fixed costs it owns
edges.resolution_rule: decide on the threshold computation at current and realistically forecast volume, with a downside year included; stay affiliated while support and supplier access are still being consumed, and move only outside a peak booking season with the portability terms already known

edges.why_related: a narrow niche builds expertise and referability but can starve a young practice of the volume its fixed costs require
edges.resolution_rule: hold the niche as the stated specialty and the direction of investment, while accepting a declared band of adjacent work until the capacity arithmetic clears fixed costs; review the band each season and shrink it as niche flow grows

edges.why_related: admitting that a client could sometimes book cheaper alone undercuts the simplest justification for a planning fee
edges.resolution_rule: never trade honesty for the fee; justify the fee on the advisory work and the specific verifiable differences the practice can actually deliver, and if that justification does not hold for a trip type, put that trip type on the fee floor or drop list instead of misrepresenting price

edges.why_related: declining or pricing small unpaid favours is financially correct but those favours often come from the very clients who generate referrals
edges.resolution_rule: apply the written per-category rule to everyone, and fund a small explicitly budgeted goodwill allowance for established clients that is counted against capacity rather than granted by whoever asks most persistently

edges.why_related: supplier standing produces the recovered bookings and genuine amenities that clients repeat to other people, which is what makes the practice referable
the ledger visibility and dispute terms found during diligence determine whether the advisor can see and query their own commission path at all
the expertise the practice claims determines which enquiries arrive, so an overstated claim manufactures misfit enquiries the decline list then has to absorb
both are jurisdictional verifications done in one pass before launch, and the registration answer often names the regulator that also answers the protection question
knowing what coverage and contracts the practice already carries is what lets diligence ask precisely what the host's arrangement adds or duplicates
what an exit would actually cost feeds straight back into how the diligence sheet weighs an attractive split against restrictive terms
measured hours and collected revenue per trip type feed back into fee floors and into which fee instrument each trip type should carry
the words referrers actually use and the communities enquiries actually arrive from are evidence that the stated niche is right, drifting or wrong
both are pre-commitment evidence routines that force a decision to rest on sourced answers rather than on an appealing pitch

conflict_axes.name: affiliation_support_vs_independent_yield
conflict_axes.description: Affiliation buys accreditation, supplier access and a support desk at the price of a share of every commission; independence keeps the full commission but converts that share into fixed costs and administrative hours the advisor personally owns.
poles: buy infrastructure with a commission share
keep the commission and own the fixed costs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide on the threshold computation at real volume with a bad year modelled, and weight the support and supplier access the practice actually consumes rather than the split alone

conflict_axes.name: headline_split_vs_exit_terms
conflict_axes.description: The most attractive commission split and the most portable contract rarely sit in the same affiliation, and the split is visible in recruitment while the exit terms are buried in clauses.
poles: optimise data ownership, notice and exit portability
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: price the exit terms into the comparison as a cost of switching, and refuse any affiliation whose data-ownership or non-solicitation language would make the practice's own book unusable

conflict_axes.name: preferred_programme_incentive_vs_brief_fit
conflict_axes.description: Programme production expectations, better commercial terms and supplier relationships all pull recommendations toward the same set of suppliers, while the client's brief may point somewhere else entirely.
poles: recommend where the programme and relationship reward the practice
recommend strictly on the client's stated brief
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the brief decides and the compensation is disclosed; where a programme benefit genuinely serves the brief, state it specifically alongside a non-preferred alternative

conflict_axes.name: niche_depth_vs_early_revenue_breadth
conflict_axes.description: Concentration is what builds expertise, supplier standing and referability, but a young practice needs bookings from wherever they arrive to clear its fixed costs.
poles: hold the niche and refuse off-profile work
take the work that pays this season
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: declare the specialty and invest only in it, while accepting a written and shrinking band of adjacent work until the capacity arithmetic clears fixed costs

conflict_axes.name: commission_only_reach_vs_fee_alignment
conflict_axes.description: Commission-only removes the price of entry for the client but pays the advisor only when the client buys, and differently depending on what they buy; a planning fee removes that pressure and adds friction instead.
poles: charge for advice to align incentives
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: match the instrument to the trip type - fee the design-heavy work whose value is the advice, keep commission-only where the booking itself is the service - and disclose either way

conflict_axes.name: compliance_verification_vs_speed_to_first_booking
conflict_axes.description: Verifying registration, licensing, entity and coverage classes takes weeks that a new practice would rather spend converting its first enquiries.
poles: verify every obligation class before selling
start selling and settle the paperwork alongside
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: obligation classes that gate the act of selling or taking money are verified first and never deferred; classes that only affect scale can be sequenced, with the decision and its date recorded

conflict_axes.name: credential_signal_vs_demonstrable_experience
conflict_axes.description: Certifications and destination designations attract enquiries and open supplier doors, but they say nothing about whether the advisor has actually been anywhere or sold anything in the niche.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy credentials after viability evidence, state plainly what each represents, and pair any genuine experience gap with the supplier or colleague who covers it

conflict_axes.name: capacity_protection_vs_client_accommodation
conflict_axes.description: Every accommodation - a rushed extra client, an unpaid favour, a trip type outside the profile - is individually reasonable and collectively the reason service quality collapses in peak season.
poles: hold the intake limit and the written policies
accommodate the client in front of you
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the limit and make accommodation explicit and budgeted, so goodwill is a decision the practice funds rather than a reflex triggered by whoever asks hardest

conflict_axes.name: price_candour_vs_persuasion
conflict_axes.description: The most effective sales moves against an online booking - implying the advisor is always cheaper, or dwelling on what could go wrong without one - are exactly the moves an honest practice cannot use.
poles: win the comparison with a strong claim
state candidly where the client can do better alone
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state which of the three price cases applies, support any advantage with a specific verifiable difference, and let the advisory value carry the rest or let the enquiry go

edge_cases.description: A trusted repeat client asks the practice to arrange a trip to a region where the advisor has no product knowledge and no supplier relationships
edge_cases.trigger: an in-profile client makes an out-of-niche request the advisor does not want to refuse
edge_cases.mitigation: say plainly that the region is outside the practice's depth, then either refer to a specialist colleague and stay in the relationship, or engage a specialist operator and disclose the arrangement and its effect on cost - never present borrowed knowledge as the practice's own

edge_cases.description: A prospect lives in a jurisdiction whose seller-of-travel regime the practice has never verified, and they want to pay a deposit this week
edge_cases.trigger: an enquiry arrives from outside the verified jurisdiction register
edge_cases.mitigation: do not take money until the class is checked against the regulator's own current publication for that jurisdiction, record the finding with its date, and if the answer cannot be obtained in time, decline or route the booking to a party that is already covered

edge_cases.description: A client asks directly whether a protection policy will cover a relative's pre-existing medical condition
edge_cases.trigger: a coverage-interpretation question is put to an advisor who may not hold the licensing class
edge_cases.mitigation: do not interpret; send the policy wording, route the question to the insurer or a licensed party, note in writing that the answer must come from them, and never fill the gap with reassurance

edge_cases.description: The host announces a revised fee and split schedule effective mid-year while the practice holds deposits for travel a year out
edge_cases.trigger: affiliation economics change under bookings that are already committed
edge_cases.mitigation: read the amendment against the contract's change clause, establish in writing which schedule applies to already-deposited bookings, re-run the threshold computation on the new terms, and treat any move as a planned transition outside peak season rather than a reaction

edge_cases.description: A supplier offers a production bonus that would apply if the practice moves a handful more bookings to them before a deadline
edge_cases.trigger: a time-limited incentive appears that could tilt recommendations
edge_cases.mitigation: add the offer to the incentive inventory, keep recommending on the brief, and if a qualifying booking is genuinely the best fit, disclose the incentive and present an alternative; never move a client's booking to hit a deadline

edge_cases.description: An adult child calls to book an expensive trip for an elderly parent who is not on the call and whose wishes are being reported second-hand
edge_cases.trigger: the payer, the traveler and the decision-maker are not the same person
edge_cases.mitigation: establish who has authority to commit funds, obtain the traveler's own confirmation where they are able to give it, send material terms in writing to the traveler as well as the payer, avoid urgency framing, and slow or decline the booking if consent cannot be established

edge_cases.description: The advisor decides to leave the host while several clients are mid-trip and others have deposits down under the host's accreditation
edge_cases.trigger: a model change lands on top of live and committed bookings
edge_cases.mitigation: map every live and deposited booking to a named handling path and support contact before announcing anything, agree in writing how post-departure travel commission is treated, and give travelers a contact route that will not break mid-trip

edge_cases.description: A long-standing client asks the advisor to rebuild an award-ticket itinerary using their own points, which pays the practice nothing
edge_cases.trigger: a valuable relationship makes a non-commissionable request
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the written per-category rule - quote the service fee or decline plainly - and if the work is absorbed as goodwill, record it against the capacity budget so the exception stays visible and finite

edge_cases.description: A client returns with a screenshot showing the same hotel and dates cheaper on a booking site
edge_cases.trigger: an online rate appears to undercut the advisor's quote
edge_cases.mitigation: compare like for like on room category, cancellation terms and inclusions, name which of the three price cases applies, and if the online option really is better, say so and let the client decide whether the advisory work is worth its fee

edge_cases.description: A close friend asks for a full itinerary as a favour, expecting the practice's normal fee to be waived
edge_cases.trigger: personal relationship pressure meets the fee policy
edge_cases.mitigation: state the standard fee and the standard scope, then decide consciously whether to gift it in whole or part, record the gift against the goodwill budget, and never let an unrecorded exception become the practice's real pricing

edge_cases.description: A consortium or host marketing push asks the practice to promote a supplier whose recent performance with the practice's own clients has been poor
edge_cases.trigger: programme marketing conflicts with firsthand experience
edge_cases.mitigation: decline to promote, record the performance evidence, raise it with the programme or supplier contact, and if the programme's core suppliers keep failing the practice's clients, treat continued membership as the decision under review

edge_cases.description: The destination at the centre of the practice's niche becomes unsellable for a season after a natural disaster or a travel advisory
edge_cases.trigger: concentration risk materialises in the chosen niche
edge_cases.mitigation: serve committed travelers first on rebooking and refunds, widen temporarily into the adjacent band already declared in the niche statement, re-run the capacity arithmetic against the reduced flow, and treat the episode as evidence in the next concentration-risk review rather than as a reason to abandon the specialty

workflow.action: State what the practice sells and how each unit of revenue comes into existence
workflow.description: Name the revenue mechanisms the practice will run on and the categories of work it will not take
workflow.gate: every named revenue mechanism has a stated payer and mechanism of arising, and at least two refused categories are listed

workflow.action: Verify the travel-seller registration obligation classes for every jurisdiction served
workflow.description: Identify the regulator, read the current requirement at source, and record the finding with its date
workflow.gate: each jurisdiction entry names the regulator, the classes checked, the source and the date, and states whether host affiliation was found to cover the obligation

workflow.action: Verify the protection-selling licensing and appointment classes before offering any protection product
workflow.description: Establish whether the practice sells, operates under another party's licence, or refers only, and write the permitted-activity script
workflow.artifact: protection activity boundary note and script
workflow.gate: the record states the classes checked with source and date, and the script defines what may be said and where every coverage question is routed

workflow.action: Stand up the entity, coverage and contract baseline
workflow.description: Establish the entity, the errors-and-omissions arrangement, the engagement terms and the client-money and record discipline
workflow.gate: for a hypothetical dispute the governing document, the responding coverage and the location of the evidence can all be named

workflow.action: Write the advice boundary and duty-of-care rules
workflow.description: Fix the routing destinations for licensed questions and the authority, consent and pacing practice for vulnerable travelers and third-party bookers
workflow.gate: each licensed question type has a named routing destination and the third-party booking sequence requires a recorded authority check and written terms

workflow.action: Choose the operating model between affiliation and independence
workflow.description: Work the threshold computation on realistic volume and decide which side of the infrastructure-for-margin trade the practice is on
workflow.artifact: model decision memo with threshold computation
workflow.gate: the memo uses the practice's own volume, contract terms and fixed-cost quotes, and includes a downside year

workflow.action: Run diligence on candidate hosts and read the exit terms before signing
workflow.description: Source every answer to a contract clause, a written reply or a named affiliate, including data ownership, notice and in-progress bookings
workflow.artifact: host comparison sheet with sourced answers
workflow.gate: no answer on the sheet is unsourced, and the exit, data-ownership and in-progress-booking terms are recorded for each candidate

workflow.action: Map the commission path for a representative itinerary
workflow.description: Record per component which accreditation identifier the booking carries, who holds the client's money and who pays whom
workflow.gate: each component names its identifier, its payment model and the counterparty to contact first if payment does not appear

workflow.action: Select a candidate niche and test it against evidence
workflow.description: Check reachable buyers, commissionable supplier density, fee tolerance, repeat rhythm and concentration risk before committing
workflow.artifact: niche viability verdict with attached evidence
workflow.gate: every claim in the verdict is attached to an observation, and the commissionable-supplier count and concentration-risk answer are both present

workflow.action: Write the served-client profile and the decline criteria
workflow.description: Describe who the practice serves in observable terms, what it declines, and how a decline is delivered
workflow.gate: the criteria are observable in a first conversation and the decline practice includes a referral or alternative

workflow.action: Design the fee model and its client explanation
workflow.description: Fix the fee instruments, what each buys, when it is charged, how it is credited, and the one-sentence explanation
workflow.gate: each instrument has a scope, a timing rule, a crediting or refund rule and a stated explanation, and the jurisdictional client-funds check has been made

workflow.action: Publish the compensation and preferred-relationship disclosure and set the intake limit
workflow.description: Inventory every incentive, put the written disclosure in front of clients before they commit, and pair it with the capacity limits the arithmetic implies
workflow.artifact: client disclosure statement and incentive inventory
workflow.gate: the disclosure is delivered before any client commitment and every preferred recommendation carries an alternative and a recorded rationale

dominance_rules.rule: Verified registration and licensing obligation classes dominate every launch, offer and enquiry decision
dominance_rules.rationale: selling or taking money outside an applicable regime can invalidate the practice's ability to trade at all, and no booking is worth that exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: an enquiry, product or jurisdiction appears that the verification register does not already cover
dominance_rules.action: stop before taking money, verify the class at the regulator's own source, record the finding with its date, and decline or route the business if the answer is not available in time

dominance_rules.rule: The licensed-advice boundary dominates client convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: a confident answer on coverage, entry rules, health or finance from an unqualified advisor harms the client and the practice more than an unsatisfying referral does
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks a question that belongs to a licensed or authoritative source
dominance_rules.action: route the question to the policy wording, the government source or the licensed professional, and record that the answer must come from them

dominance_rules.rule: The client's brief dominates every compensation difference
dominance_rules.rationale: an advisory practice survives on trust, and a recommendation that cannot be defended on the client's own stated terms is steering however profitable it is
dominance_rules.trigger: a preferred programme, bonus, override or split difference would change which option is recommended
dominance_rules.action: recommend on the brief, disclose the incentive in writing, and present a credible alternative with the rationale recorded

dominance_rules.rule: Written disclosure before commitment dominates conversion pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: the damage from a client discovering an undisclosed incentive after the fact is permanent, while the friction of disclosing early is temporary
dominance_rules.trigger: a client is about to commit money without having received the compensation and programme disclosure
dominance_rules.action: deliver the disclosure first and delay the commitment until it has been sent

dominance_rules.rule: Contract exit and data-ownership terms dominate the headline commission split
dominance_rules.rationale: a split affects margin per booking while portability decides whether the practice's client base is an asset it owns at all
dominance_rules.trigger: one candidate host offers a better split and worse data-ownership, notice or non-solicitation terms
dominance_rules.action: weight the exit terms as a switching cost and refuse terms that would make the practice's own book unusable, regardless of the split

dominance_rules.rule: Vulnerable-traveler care dominates speed, urgency and volume
dominance_rules.rationale: consent, comprehension and authority cannot be repaired after the deposit, and a lost hold costs less than a booking the traveler never truly agreed to
dominance_rules.trigger: signs of confusion or frailty, a third party booking on someone's behalf, or a commitment large relative to what the traveler has described
dominance_rules.action: slow the process, confirm authority, obtain the traveler's own confirmation where possible, send material terms in writing, and drop any urgency framing

dominance_rules.rationale: a single discovered exaggeration about price destroys the credibility that every future recommendation depends on
dominance_rules.trigger: a client comparison where the online or loyalty option is genuinely equal or better
dominance_rules.action: say so plainly, state what the advisory work adds, and accept losing the enquiry rather than misrepresenting the comparison

dominance_rules.rule: The intake limit dominates revenue temptation
dominance_rules.rationale: accepting past capacity damages clients already paid for and the referral base that took years to build
dominance_rules.trigger: a new enquiry arrives when the period is already at the limit the capacity arithmetic set
dominance_rules.action: decline, waitlist to a later window, or refer out, rather than absorbing the work and degrading service on existing bookings

dominance_rules.rule: Evidence of niche viability dominates the advisor's enthusiasm
dominance_rules.rationale: a niche with no reachable buyers or no commissionable suppliers cannot be rescued by passion, credentials or marketing spend
dominance_rules.trigger: a niche decision, credential purchase or programme membership is proposed without viability evidence
dominance_rules.action: hold the spend until the viability verdict exists with its evidence attached

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the registration and protection-licensing classes before building the offer, the website or any advertising
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rewriting client-facing material, unwinding bookings or refunding fees taken under an unverified regime

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the exit, data-ownership and in-progress-booking terms before signing an affiliation, not when leaving one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at departure that the practice's own client records and pipeline belong to someone else

anti_rework_rules.rule: Test niche viability before buying credentials, joining programmes or declaring a specialty publicly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sunk certification and membership spend keyed to a niche the practice then abandons, plus a public claim that has to be walked back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the served-client profile and the decline criteria before marketing anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a pipeline of misfit enquiries that consume design hours and then have to be declined late and awkwardly

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the fee model, its scope and its explanation before quoting the first client
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inconsistent pricing between clients that surfaces the moment two of them compare notes, and unpaid design work absorbed by default

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map the commission path for each product type before promising service on components of an itinerary
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committing hours to components that pay nothing and chasing the wrong counterparty when money does not arrive

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the compensation and preferred-relationship disclosure before joining a programme or accepting an incentive
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retrofitting disclosure onto client relationships that were formed without it, which reads as an admission rather than a policy

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the intake limit and the goodwill budget before the first referral wave arrives
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a peak season where every accepted accommodation is individually reasonable and service quality collapses collectively

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put engagement terms and the coverage arrangement in place before accepting any client money
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scope and refund arguments fought without a governing document, and coverage gaps discovered during a claim

iteration_protocol.trigger: the practice takes an enquiry from a jurisdiction not on the verification register, or a regulator amends a requirement
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the registration and protection-licensing verification for that jurisdiction, record the finding with its date, and hold client money until it is answered

iteration_protocol.trigger: the host amends its fee schedule, split tiers, service levels or contract terms
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the threshold computation and the diligence comparison on the new terms and re-price the exit cost before reacting

iteration_protocol.trigger: niche enquiry flow stays thin through a full seasonal cycle, or the commissionable-supplier assumption proves wrong
iteration_protocol.action: re-open the viability test with fresh observations and either adjust the axes or widen the declared adjacent band before spending further on the niche

iteration_protocol.trigger: fee resistance clusters in one client type, enquiry source or trip type
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine what the fee buys and how it is explained before changing its level, and check whether the trip type belongs above the fee floor at all

iteration_protocol.trigger: referrals arrive describing the practice in words that do not match the stated specialty
iteration_protocol.action: compare the referrers' language and sources against the designed surface and correct either the description or the niche statement

iteration_protocol.trigger: turnaround times slip, revisions pile up, or a client notices a lapse in attention
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as an intake-limit breach, re-measure hours per trip type, and tighten intake or raise the fee floor before quality damage reaches the referral base

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new incentive appears, or an audit of proposals shows one supplier dominating regardless of brief
iteration_protocol.action: add the incentive to the inventory, refresh the client disclosure, and review the recommendation rationales that produced the pattern

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client dispute, family objection or complaint suggests the consent or expectation-setting practice was too loose
iteration_protocol.action: review the advice-boundary routing and the written-confirmation sequence for the client group involved and tighten the pacing rules

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the practice cannot judge an affiliation, a niche or a fee until it has said what it sells and which registration, licensing, entity and advice-boundary obligations bind it; the model nodes follow because whose accreditation a booking is written under determines the commission path, the supplier access and the exit terms that everything commercial rests on; the niche nodes come next because concentration is what converts a model into supplier standing, a referral surface and a definable client; and the economics nodes come last because fee design, disclosure, non-commissionable policy, price honesty and capacity limits can only be set once the model, the niche and the money path they act on are known.
